c74object.name: bachmcp.shmbuffer~
c74object.digest: Samples in shared memory, for Python to read and write
c74object.description: Holds samples in a POSIX shared memory object, /bachmcp.<name>, so that another program, notably Python (ShmBuffer in py/bach_mcp/utilities/shmbuffer.py), works on the very same memory: nothing is written to disk and nothing is sent. source fills the memory from a buffer~ or a sound file; bang puts it into a buffer~ (target, or one the object makes) and sends that buffer~'s name out of the left outlet. When Python changes the samples and says so (touch(), write()), the object hears it, and with notify 1 writes its buffer~ by itself. Whenever Max changes the memory, Python can hear it too (wait()). No audio: to play or show the samples, write them to a buffer~.

inlet.digest: bang: the memory into a buffer~; source, target, size, write, set_name, info

outlet.digest: The name of the buffer~ just written

objarg.name: name
objarg.description: The memory is /bachmcp.<name>: at most 22 characters (macOS allows 31 with the prefix), no slash. With a name only, the object joins the memory if a program already made it, or makes an empty one.

objarg.name: ms
objarg.description: With a duration, the object makes a new, silent memory of this size, replacing what was under the name, at Max's sample rate.

objarg.name: channels
objarg.description: The channels of the new memory, 1 (default) to 1024.

method.name: bang
method.digest: Write the memory to a buffer~
method.description: Writes the memory into target, resized to the memory's frames, channels and sample rate; with no target, into a buffer~ the object makes on first need, with a unique name. Then a bang out of the right outlet and the buffer~'s name out of the left one.

method.name: source
method.digest: Read a buffer~ or a sound file into the memory, now
method.description: The same as source, and it reads it at once.

method.name: target
method.digest: Write the memory into a buffer~, now
method.description: The same as target, and it writes at once. Alone: no target; bang writes the object's own buffer~ again.

method.name: size
method.digest: New, silent memory of this duration
method.description: A new memory of this many ms at the memory's sample rate, with these channels (default: as they were). macOS can't resize a shared memory: a new size is a new memory under the same name, which Python follows by itself.

method.name: sizeinsamps
method.digest: New, silent memory of this many frames

method.name: sr
method.digest: Sample rate written in the memory
method.description: Sets the sample rate held in the memory's header; the samples are left as they are.

method.name: set_name
method.description: The object goes to this name. A memory already there: it joins it. None: the samples come along to the new name, and the old memory is removed if this object made it. name is the same.

method.name: info
method.description: Out of the right outlet, one message each: name, shm (the name for shm_open), frames, channels, sr, ms, serial (raised by whoever changes the memory).

method.name: write
method.digest: Write the memory into a sound file
method.description: As buffer~ does: the format comes from the extension (.wav .aif .caf .flac; none: .wav), the sample type from samptype. No file: a save dialog. A bare name goes next to the patcher. Then written <path> out of the right outlet.

attribute.name: source
attribute.description: A buffer~ or a sound file (any format macOS reads: absolute, Disk:/..., or a name in Max's search path); a buffer~ of that name wins. The memory takes its format: frames, channels, sample rate, whatever the arguments. Given as an argument, it is read once the patcher is loaded, so the buffer~ may come later in the patch.

attribute.name: target
attribute.digest: The buffer~ the samples go to
attribute.description: The buffer~ bang writes into, resized to fit the memory. None: a buffer~ of the object's own.

attribute.name: notify
attribute.digest: Write when Python says it changed the samples
attribute.description: 1: when the other program announces a change (in Python: touch() or write(), which post the Darwin notification bachmcp.shmbuffer.<name>), do as for bang. Nothing is polled: a change nobody announces is not seen. Either way, the Max console says python written <name>.

c74object.discussion: The memory is a 64-byte header, then float32 samples interleaved by channel, as in a buffer~ (layout in sources/bachmcp.shmbuffer~/source/bachmcp.shmbuffer.h). In Python: buf = ShmBuffer("name"); buf.array is the samples themselves, float32, frames x channels; buf.touch() says they changed; buf.write(samples, sr) replaces them (another size: a new memory); buf.wait() sleeps until Max changes the memory (source, size, sizeinsamps, sr, clear). There is no lock: two programs writing at once get a mix of both. The memory is removed when the object that made it is freed; a retyped box or a reopened patch keeps it. Messages run in the main thread. examples/python/shmbuffers.py, run by bachmcp.python, shows the Python side.
